title: Sebastian and the Postcard
premise: Rafael Sandoval, a pastry chef whose café is three missed payments from gone, signs up for an anonymous pen-pal program meant to drum up festival business — only to be paired, by clerical error, with her bitterest rival: the developer threatening to buy her block. Writing as strangers, they fall for each other's words before either knows the truth. When the deception surfaces at the harvest festival, Rafael must choose between the safe, rationed heart she has always kept in the past tense and the whole, reckless one that could save both her café and her future.
about_author: Juniper Ishikawa is a former bakery counter girl who writes love stories set in kitchens, post offices, and other places where people linger too long. She lives in a coastal town where every autumn festival smells like cinnamon and second chances.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Facing foreclosure notices and the demolition threat from Marlowe Development, Rafael grudgingly joins the town's anonymous pen-pal festival program to draw customers. Her first letter goes out; a witty, warm reply arrives from 'A.' The beat: guarded hope flickering inside exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Stranger Who Knows My Coffee
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Rafael and Adrian Marlowe, who realizes mid-correspondence that his pen pal is the woman whose café he's been sent to acquire — and hides it. Their letters deepen while their daytime encounters sharpen into open hostility. The beat: dramatic irony tightening like a wire.

chapters.title: What the Postcard Said
chapters.summary: Adrian's POV, then Rafael's. A misdelivered postcard reveals the truth: her beloved stranger is her enemy. At the festival eve meeting where pen pals finally meet, Rafael sees him holding her letter and shatters publicly. Adrian withdraws the development offer, losing everything. The beat: betrayal, heartbreak, and the cost of survival laid bare.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. With the café saved but her trust in ruins, Rafael finds Adrian's final unsent letter — honest, unstrategic, terrified. On the festival's last night she chooses risk over safety, reading her own confession aloud from the stage. He steps out of the crowd. The beat: belonging won not by rescue, but by her own brave hand.
